sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from FY2017 to FY2026, reaching $67.4 billion from $37.8 billion [F196][F1][F10].
The window is not a smooth compounder: revenue grew 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026, against 0.3% in FY2019 and -1.1% in FY2020 [D280][D421][D97][D143].
The FY2023 step came primarily from revenue contributions from the Cerner acquisition, which added $5.9 billion, 11.8% of that year's revenue [P48][S61][D604].

The FY2026 step came from cloud revenues as customers purchased applications and infrastructure technologies and renewed cloud contracts, with cloud infrastructure contributing 84% of constant-currency cloud growth [P17][P20].
Cloud Infrastructure is the largest latest-year driver: revenue of $18.1 billion, 26.9% of total, growing 76.9% and contributing 13.7pp of the 17.3% revenue growth [S92][D643][D644][D645][D421].
Cloud Applications added 2.8pp on 11.3% growth to $15.9 billion, while Software License fell 8.9% and subtracted 0.8pp [D668][D667][S101][D681][D682].
The Americas contributed 14.2pp of FY2026 growth and now supply 66.0% of revenue, against 2.9pp from other countries [D470][D468][D502].
Operating costs grew 0.3pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 17.7%, after growing 2.8pp slower in FY2025 [D443][D436][D396].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against net income growth of 36.5% as the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well below the 37.6% FY2021 high, but above the 25.7% FY2022 low [F34][D788][D787][D786].
The FY2026 margin slipped 0.2pp as cloud and software total margin fell on higher infrastructure expenses to support cloud infrastructure growth [D433][P16].
R&D fell to 15.3% of revenue and added 1.9pp to margin, while other lines subtracted 2.1pp [D399][D444][D445].
In FY2026 net margin of 25.2% sat 5.4pp below the 30.6% operating margin, a narrower gap than the 9.1pp of FY2025 [F54][F34][D832][D831].
Operating cash flow of $32.0 billion was 1.88x net income, above the 1.58x window median [F84][D408][D822].

That increase was primarily due to higher net income adjusted for non-cash charges and favorable working capital, including $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, as capex of $55.7 billion reached 82.6% of revenue and 7.30x D&A [F104][D405][F94][D404][D410].
Investing outflows rose $30.1 billion primarily on a $34.4 billion increase in capital expenditures [P5].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion, net cash of -145.0% of revenue against a -0.5% software peer median, the 0th percentile of six peers [D414][D415][D816][D815].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion as the company issued $42.7 billion of senior notes and $5.0 billion of mandatory convertible preferred [D440][D413][P7].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover 1.3 years of the latest burn, and the current ratio of 1.12x sits below the 1.96x window median [D412][D419][F184][D803].
Buybacks plus dividends of $5.9 billion were paid while free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, and the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D416][F104][D438].
Free cash flow turned negative in FY2025 and FY2026, at -0.03x and -1.39x net income, far below the 1.06x window median [D362][D409][D800].
The capex build is the swing factor, so cash generation now depends on whether the data-center spend converts into cloud revenue [D404].
Net debt rose for a second year to $97.6 billion, with total debt up 39.9% in FY2026 [D320][D367][D414][D440].
Leverage is now the balance-sheet constraint, and interest expense of $4.6 billion will rise with the new borrowings [X92][P10].
The FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure of $17.1 billion by up to 0.60% [F44][X20][R5].
The gap is small but means margin and EPS figures for FY2026 should be read against the 10-K value where precision matters [X20].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the -35.2% FY2026 level, in the FY2027 10-K [D405].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -145.0% or extends the two-year rise in net debt, in the FY2027 10-K [D415][D367].
Whether operating margin holds above the 30.6% FY2026 level or falls toward the 25.7% window low, in the FY2027 10-K [F34][D786].
